result.source_concept: head chef in a restaurant kitchen

mappings.relation: central coordinating entity that manages overall operation
mappings.evidence: The analogy opens with "The CPU is the Head Chef... central figure ensuring the kitchen runs smoothly".

mappings.target_element: program instructions delivered to the CPU
mappings.relation: provides the tasks or orders to be executed
mappings.evidence: "The chef (CPU) receives orders from the waitstaff (the instructions from programs)".

mappings.source_element: chopping, mixing, cooking actions using tools
mappings.target_element: arithmetic and logic operations performed by the ALU
mappings.relation: executes core operational work using specialized mechanisms
mappings.evidence: "For chopping, mixing, or cooking ... the chef uses specific tools and techniques (the ALU)".

mappings.target_element: CPU control unit coordinating internal components
mappings.relation: orchestrates timing and sequencing of sub‑tasks
mappings.evidence: "The chef also coordinates the kitchen staff ... (the control unit)".

mappings.source_element: sending completed dishes to the dining area
mappings.relation: delivers final results to external recipients
mappings.evidence: "The chef ensures the completed dishes are sent out to the dining area (input/output operations)".

result.process_summary: Both the head chef and the CPU act as central managers: they receive orders, interpret them, perform core work using specialized subsystems (tools/ALU), coordinate subordinate agents (kitchen staff/control unit), and finally deliver the finished product to the outside world (dishes/I‑O).
potential_breaks: A chef is a conscious human capable of creativity, whereas a CPU follows deterministic logic.
Kitchen staff are distinct individuals; the CPU's internal units are not autonomous agents.
Cooking transforms raw ingredients physically, while CPU operations manipulate abstract data.
